newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, gold mostly up.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, gold mostly up.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mixed on Friday in moderate trade, rebounding from early lows after the yen retreated against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ended mostly up. Benchmark June was up one yen per gram at 1,233 yen.
"In gold futures, private investors generally hunted for bargains, but further gains would be limited on expected profit-taking," one analyst at a commodity broker said.
Spot gold was quoted weaker at $336.90/337.40 per ounce at 0724 GMT, against $338.00/338.50 in New York on Thursday.
Traders said spot gold is unlikely to stray from its range between $336 and $340 per ounce, but will continue to be overshadowed by producer selling and possible European central bank gold sales.
Expectations that Asian gold demand may experience a seasonal fall in summer, also dampened sentiment, they said.
Platinum group metals (PGMs) were mostly firmer.

"Although private investors have built fresh shorts especially in palladium, sentiment remains firm due to massive short-positions (equivalent of 52.5 tonnes as of Thursday) and the shortage of the metals," one trader said.

Traders expect Japan's PGM imports for June to fall sharply after Finance Ministry data today showed PGM imports for May fell. "End-users, loathing the high prices and expecting Russian spot sales to resume soon, have refrained from buying supplies in June," one trader said.
"Although we are expecting contracted Russian supplies to arrive in early July, the domestic palladium market is currently very tight," he said.
Benchmark June platinum was up four yen at 1,360 yen and benchmark June palladium was down four yen at 496 yen. Benchmark June silver was up 0.1 yen per 10 grams at 176.7 yen.
